rules.title: An assertion defends observable behaviour
rules.text: A test earns its place by failing on a plausible bug. A length that grew, a value that is merely non-empty, a call that did not panic, or an assertion that the code echoed what the test supplied defends the implementation rather than the contract.

judgement.question: Does this assertion defend what a consumer observes — a value, a boundary, an exit code, an ordering — or is it plumbing: a length that grew, a non-empty check, a bare did-not-fail, or an echo of what the test itself supplied?

criteria.true: the assertion passes for any implementation that produces something — `!value.is_empty()`, a length that grew, a bare `is_ok()`, an assertion that a mock echoed what the test handed it — and nothing in it can distinguish a wrong implementation from a right one
criteria.false: the assertion pins something a consumer depends on: a value, an error, a boundary, an ordering, or a count that is itself the contract
